subject: Re: Atlas AI — clarification on per-token billing & commit tiers
messages:
From: Sarah Kim <sarah@atlasai.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@atlasai.com
Date: 2026-02-11T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Clarification on per-token billing (streaming tokens + rounding) and commit tiers

Ben — thanks for the earlier call. Procurement and engineering dug into the draft SOW and pricing spreadsheet. A couple of things we need explicit clarity on before legal will sign: 1) how you define "billable tokens" for streaming endpoints (are partial chunks billed? counted when emitted?). 2) do you round per-call, per-stream-chunk, or per-day? We've simulated at Atlas and streaming chat can inflate nominal counts by ~6-9% depending on chunking. 3) how do commit tiers and the true-up work — is the discount applied to actual usage after rounding, or to committed quantity only?

High-level asks from procurement: a model of monthly committed units with quarterly true-ups, and contract language that ties billing to your tokenization library (so we can reconcile). Also: can you provide a short clause we can drop into our PO?

Appreciate quick clarity — we have a February 18 target for legal sign-off.

—Sarah
Sarah Kim
Head of Platform, Atlas AI

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Kim <sarah@atlasai.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: 2026-02-11T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Clarification on per-token billing (streaming tokens + rounding) and commit tiers

Hi Sarah — thanks, this is a great set of questions. Summary answers up front, then a suggested contract clause and our alternate options below.

1) Billable tokens: We measure billable tokens using the same tokenizer library we ship with the runtime (Redwood BPE v2). Billable tokens = prompt_tokens + generated_tokens as emitted by the tokenizer. For streaming endpoints we count tokens as they are emitted by the server (so partial progress is not invoiced until token boundaries are reached by the tokenizer).

2) Rounding: By default we apply per-request rounding up to the nearest 10 tokens to reduce microbilling noise (this applies to both non-streaming and streaming requests; streaming uses the same per-emitted-token accounting, then the per-request total is rounded at the end of the call). We can change rounding to per-token (no rounding), per-1 token, or per-100 token buckets by contract.

3) Commit tiers / true-up: Commit tiers are monthly committed token volumes. Discounts apply to the invoiced (billed) usage after rounding. True-ups happen quarterly — if billed usage is below committed quantity we'll credit the over-commit on the next invoice; if over committed we bill the incremental usage at the discounted rate corresponding to the tier reached that month.

Suggested contract language (drop-in):
"Billable Units and Rounding. Billable Units for all Hosted API calls shall be determined using Redwoods Redwood BPE v2 tokenizer. For each API call, Billable Units shall equal the number of prompt tokens plus the number of generated tokens as reported by Redwoods tokenizer. For streaming endpoints, tokens shall be counted when emitted by the service and aggregated for the call. For billing purposes, the total Billable Units for each API call will be rounded up to the nearest 10 tokens unless otherwise specified in the Order Form.

Commit and True-up. Customer may elect a Monthly Commitment of Billable Units in the Order Form. The elected discount tier will apply to Billed Usage (after rounding) for the applicable billing period. Quarterly, Redwood will reconcile actual Billed Usage against the Customer's Monthly Commitment and issue credits or additional charges to align invoicing with committed volumes. Credits shall be applied to the subsequent invoice."

I've attached an updated pricing sheet that shows sample tier bands and the math (redwood_pricing_sheet_Q1_v3.xlsx). If you want tighter math we can remove the rounding clause and bill per-token. That would require a small per-token price increase to account for microbilling and reporting costs.

Next steps: if procurement is OK with rounding-to-10 we can lock the Order Form; otherwise we can propose a hybrid: rounding-to-1 token for requests < 256 tokens and rounding-to-10 for larger calls (minimizes short-chat noise).

—Ben

Looping in finance and legal — quick note from our side. Marcus, Evelyn: we should give Atlas the option for 1) "per-token billing" (no rounding) or 2) "bucketed rounding" (nearest 10) in the Order Form. If they pick per-token, propose a 3% premium on unit price to account for reporting and microbilling. Also recommend adding a usage feed (S3/CSV) that publishes tokenized counts per-call daily so Atlas can reconcile autonomously.

Sarah: one other operational point — we'll add an explicit definition of "streaming chunk" in the SOW to avoid ambiguity. Marcus can you draft the feed spec?

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

From: procurement@atlasai.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: 2026-02-12T10:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Clarification on per-token billing (streaming tokens + rounding) and commit tiers

Thanks — procurement reviewed the suggested language. A few asks before we can sign: 1) Can you limit the rounding-to-10 clause to calls whose total billable tokens exceed 512 to avoid penalizing small requests? 2) For streaming, we need explicit language that tokens are counted at tokenizer boundaries and that partial bytes are not billed. 3) We require a daily usage CSV (S3 link) that includes: request_id, timestamp, model, prompt_tokens, generated_tokens, total_billable_tokens (post-rounding), and zone. This will be used for our reconciliation.

Can you provide the S3 spec and an invoice sample showing a quarter true-up? Also, for the true-up: will credits have an expiry? We need that in the PO (suggest 12 months).

—Procurement (on behalf of Atlas AI)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Kim <sarah@atlasai.com>, procurement@atlasai.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: 2026-02-12T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Clarification on per-token billing (streaming tokens + rounding) and commit tiers

Sarah / Procurement — thanks, we can accommodate the asks. Confirmations and next steps below: 

• Rounding: we'll change the clause to: "Rounding to nearest 10 tokens applies only when total Billable Units for a call exceed 512 tokens; otherwise billing will be per-token (no rounding)."
• Streaming: tokens are counted at tokenizer token boundaries; partial bytes not billed. We'll add the exact tokenizer repo/version in the SOW.
• Usage feed: we'll publish a daily CSV to a customer-owned S3 bucket (or a Redwood-provided bucket with cross-account access). Schema: request_id, timestamp_utc, model, prompt_tokens, generated_tokens, pre_rounding_total, post_rounding_total, region. See attached usage_feed_spec.csv.
• True-up credits: Redwood agrees to 12-month expiry on credits issued via true-up.

I've attached the updated commit tiers document (proposed_commit_tiers_redwood.docx) and the usage feed spec. If this looks good, we'll have legal incorporate the revised clause and route DocuSign for the Order Form. I'll also upload a sample invoice showing a quarterly true-up to the HubSpot deal page (link above).

Proposed immediate action: legal teams exchange a single redline to the Order Form by EOD Friday (2026-02-13). If you prefer, we can set up a short call to walk the clause live.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
attachments: proposed_commit_tiers_redwood.docx, usage_feed_spec.csv, redwood_pricing_sheet_Q1_v3.xlsx
